deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is an instrument calibration page from Gauss's Göttingen observatory work, around 1819. The previous page contains the 1819 entries and a list headed 'Empfindlichkeit einiger Libellen' (sensitivity of several levels).

(1) Header: 'Hängelibelle zu Reichenbachs Kreise', the hanging (striding) level of the Reichenbach circle.
- Scale value: one level part is 1p = 1.84843''.
- Linear value: 1'' of tilt moves the bubble 1.226 mm.
- Implied length of one part (my inference): 1p ≈ 1.84843 × 1.226 ≈ 2.266 mm. This is about one Paris line (2.2558 mm). The previous page likewise says 'Die Theile sind par. Linien' for the main level of the same circle.

(2) Zenith distances of a tree top close to the meridian ('nahe am M.'), presumably used as a terrestrial mark.
- True zenith distance: 89°7'46''.
- Measured with the Reichenbach circle, 'O.' (probably circle East or object-glass position): 89°37'9''.
- No reduction is written. The difference of 29'23'' is presumably an index/zero-point error of the circle reading in that position (my inference).

(3) Table 'Correction wegen Ausschlag der Libelle am Kreise', i.e. correction of the circle reading for the bubble's deflection. Argument: 'Dopp. Aussch.', the double deflection, meaning the difference of the end readings in the two positions, in level parts. Result: a correction in arcseconds.
- Entries for arguments 0 to 14: 0, 0.73, 1.47, 2.20, 2.94, 3.67, 4.40, 5.13, 5.85, 6.57, 7.29, 8.00, 8.71, 9.42, 10.12.
- First differences: 0.73, 0.74, 0.73, 0.74, 0.73, 0.73, 0.73, 0.72, 0.72, 0.72, 0.71, 0.71, 0.71, 0.70. They decrease slowly, so the relation is close to linear (about 0.735''/part near zero) but slightly concave.
- The table is then continued in inverse form: the double deflection needed to give round corrections. 21.148 → 15'', 28.924 → 20'', 37.257 → 25'', 46.224 → 30''.
- Mean ratio correction/argument: 0.735 (small x), 0.723 (x=14), 0.709 (21.1), 0.691 (28.9), 0.671 (37.3), 0.649 (46.2).
- So the scale value of the bubble run decreases along the tube. This is an empirical calibration of a non-uniformly curved vial, tabulated by interpolation. It is not a closed-form formula.
- The factor 0.73 is not simply half of 1.84843 (0.924). The table therefore refers either to a different level (the circle's level 'am Kreise', not the hanging level) or to a reduction convention not stated on the page.

(4) 'Südl. M. Z. im O. Spalt 0°4'15''9': a zenith-distance-type reading or offset for the southern meridian mark seen through the eastern slit, about 4'15.9''. It is recorded with no derivation.
errors: No arithmetic error can be established. The table's internal differences are smooth and monotone.

Minor inconsistency, only if 'p' means a Paris line (2.2558 mm): then 1'' = 2.2558/1.84843 = 1.2204 mm, not 1.226 mm. The 0.5% discrepancy suggests the two numbers come from separate determinations, or p is not exactly a Paris line.
The coefficient ~0.735''/part in the correction table is not explained on the page. It is not half of the hanging level's 1.84843''/p, so the table is for a different level or convention.

results.what: Scale value of the Reichenbach circle's hanging level: 1p = 1.84843'', 1'' = 1.226 mm
results.usually_credited_to: Standard observatory practice (Reichenbach, Bessel, Struve and others in the early 19th century)

results.what: Nonlinear table converting the level's double deflection into a correction in arcseconds, extended by inverse interpolation (15'', 20'', 25'', 30'')
results.modern_name: Empirical level calibration / correction table (non-uniform vial curvature)
results.usually_credited_to: Routine practice; level testers ('Libellenprüfer') were later standard

results.what: True versus measured zenith distance of a terrestrial mark (tree top) and a meridian-mark reading

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine instrument-calibration bookkeeping (level scale values, an empirical correction table, mark zenith distances) for Gauss's Reichenbach meridian circle at Göttingen around 1819. Gauss's use of these instruments is well documented, and no new mathematics appears.

checkable.asserts: One level part ≈ 1 Paris line (2.2558 mm) given 1p=1.84843'' and 1''=1.226 mm (agreement to about 0.5%)
mm per arcsecond if p is exactly a Paris line (≈1.2204, versus the written 1.226)
First differences of the correction table decrease slowly from ~0.74 to 0.70 (slightly concave relation)
Mean scale value falls from ~0.723 to ~0.649 ''/part as deflection grows, confirming the table is nonlinear

transcription_corrections: Header reads 'Hängelibelle zu Reichenb[ach]s Kreise' (the transcription is fine). 1p = 1''84843 and 1'' = 1mm226 are confirmed from the image.
Line 2 reads 'mit R. gemessen ... O. 89.37.9'. The '[?]' below it is a faint scribble ('All'?) of no substance.

In the last table rows the left column (21,148; 28.924; 37.257; 46.224) is the double deflection and the right column (15, 20, 25, 30) the correction. The columns are reversed relative to the upper part (an inverse table); the transcription order is right, but this should be noted.
Bottom note reads 'Südl. M. Z. im O. Spalt' (probably 'Südl[iche] M[ire] Z[enithdistanz]' or 'Mittags-Zeichen', eastern slit): 0°4'15''9.
